improvements.title: Select the anti-rollback backend: HDP1-hidden unary flash-page counter owned by the pre-PIN stage (Trezor monoctr shape on the same silicon) instead of the stalled OTP codec
improvements.threat: Validly-signed downgrade to a vulnerable release. Today the floor can never move past its factory value: otp::bump_to has zero call sites, COMMIT refuses unconditionally, and the only selected physical backend (OTP quad-words) is invalid on STM32U585 ECC OTP, leaving every release the vendor ever signed installable forever (#31 ship-blocker).
improvements.proposal: Take an owner decision to route OPEN-OTP-1..3 to a non-OTP backend: one 8 KB bank-1 flash page per counter (security_epoch; optionally a second for release_version), encoded exactly as Trezor monoctr: value N == first N 16-byte quad-words programmed to 0x00, read rejects any programmed-after-erased gap, write refuses values below current and programs one fresh QW per increment with write->read->ensure, MONOCTR_MAX static-asserted against the largest epoch any release may carry. Place the page(s) at the start of the bank-1 secure area so HDP1 (SECWM1R2.HDP1EN + HDP1_PEND) covers FSBL pages 0..4 plus the counter page(s); the pre-PIN stage reads/bumps them, then sets FLASH_SECHDPCR.HDP1_ACCDIS before branching, so the mutable secure runtime can neither read nor forge the floor. Keep the counter page OUTSIDE the WRP range (WRP prevents the increment; Trezor's secret sector is pages 0-1 while WRP covers 2-13). Close #212 (OPTIGA E1E0 layer) as 'not needed' once this lands, and fold #39 (HDP1) into it.
improvements.rationale: This is the single most relevant vendor finding: Trezor solved the identical problem on the identical flash controller by moving the unary tally from OTP (F4) to an HDP-hidden ordinary page (U5), which U585 supports natively (one-shot QW programming, page erase only pre-lock, HDP temporal hiding until reset). It dissolves OPEN-OTP-1..3's 'one-program-only, interrupted program not retry-safe' blocker because a torn QW simply reads as programmed, and an 8 KB page gives 512 increments versus 64 QWs of OTP. It also gives invariant #10's FSBL an actual enforcement lever for the floor the runtime cannot lower even when fully compromised.

improvements.title: FI-harden the FSBL's SPHINCS+C10 VERIFIER against the WOTS checksum/target-sum fault class, give the FSBL a real TRNG for wait_random, and make the branch target default-to-fail
improvements.threat: A single laser/voltage fault during boot-time or BEGIN-time signature verification accepts a forged firmware signature (Wagner et al. PQCrypto 2023; BSI/AISEC LFI 2025 on an ordinary MCU). In WOTS+C the 'checksum' is the target-sum check, and it is a single bare compare on the verify path; the FSBL verifies once, its retiming jitter is a constant, and the final branch reads the reset vector of whichever slot enum value survives.
improvements.proposal: (a) Inside sphincs_c10 verify: recompute the digit sum from a second extraction of the digest, route `sum == TARGET_SUM` and the forced-zero FORS constraint through a Hamming-distant sentinel (pqsigner_fi::check_true_into_sentinel) with black_box, and gate chain-length derivation on the sentinel; (b) in the FSBL, verify the manifest signature twice with an independent recomputed root compared constant-time (redundant-recomputation, the same discipline c10_sign_verified already applies to signing), or at minimum re-verify the chosen candidate once more immediately before `into_slot`; (c) initialise the STM32U585 TRNG in the FSBL (RCC AHB2 RNG clock + GTZC RNG secure bit, the same pattern fsbl/src/hash.rs uses for HASH) so wait_random is attacker-unpredictable; (d) in fsbl/src/branch.rs keep the branch address in a sentinel-encoded register initialised to a halt stub and overwritten only after the chosen slot's `img_ok_*` is re-confirmed, so a fault that flips the `Slot` enum cannot land in the unverified slot; (e) run the rainbow instruction-skip/stuck-at sweeps for fsbl::filter_valid, fsbl::verify_images and the CHUNK->COMMIT window (#591, #633).
improvements.rationale: The signer is covered by double-compute, but a national-agency-backed practical LFI result targets VERIFICATION of hash-based signatures, and pq1's FSBL verifier is the one component that can never be patched after RDP-2. The outer sentinel wraps only the boolean result of a single verify; a fault inside wots.rs:178 makes the verify return the attacker's chosen root, which the outer gate then happily accepts. Trezor's boardloader uses TRNG-seeded fih_delay before every ensure and a default-fail jump pointer; pq1's FSBL has neither.

improvements.title: Bind the board model and hardware revision into the signed manifest preimage and check it at BEGIN and in the FSBL (the #487 trigger has fired: two boards exist)
improvements.threat: A validly-signed iota2 image installed on pq1 silicon (or vice-versa) via the companion or a swapped .pqfw. On pq1, PA8 is LDO2_EN — the rail enable for BOTH secure elements — while on iota2 it is the RIGHT button; the wrong pin map is physically dangerous and the signature does not prevent it because nothing in the preimage says which board the image is for.
improvements.proposal: Add `hw_model` (4-byte tag, e.g. b"PQ1A" / b"IOTA") and `hw_revision` (u16) to the Draft 1.1 V6 signed preimage (owner spec amendment: 121 -> 127 bytes, new digest), bake the expected pair into both the FSBL and the secure image (same allocated-section pattern as `.pqsigner.vendor_pubkey`), and reject on mismatch BEFORE the expensive C10 verify in both `fw_update::verify_manifest` and `fsbl::filter_valid`. fwsign refuses to sign without `--hw-model`, and the release gate cross-checks the model tag against the ELF's `board-*` feature. Until V6 lands, add the same check as an unsigned fast-reject on V1 plus a `make release` refusal, documented as non-authoritative.
improvements.rationale: Trezor signs hw_model and hw_revision in every header and refuses before signature verification; the boardloader additionally exports board_capabilities so firmware will not stage a bootloader for a different board. pq1 made board selection MANDATORY at build time precisely because a silent wrong pin map put iota2 pins on pq1 silicon once already (CLAUDE.md, 2026-08-31 retraction) — the update path has no equivalent guard, and the V6 draft, which is the only place a new signed field can go, was frozen without one.

improvements.title: Verify the unused tail of each slot is erased (0xFF) at COMMIT and at every FSBL boot, and sign the image lengths
improvements.threat: Stale bytes from a previous image, or bytes planted by a hostile companion/implant in the slack after `len`, survive in the inactive slot and can be referenced by a crafted (but validly signed) image or by a later torn update; combined with unsigned lengths in V1 this is the 'firmware must not be compressible / spare flash must be unusable' assumption Donjon used to bypass Trezor's Suite hash check.
improvements.proposal: COMMIT: after verify_images, walk `[slot_base + received_len, slot_base + capacity)` for both halves and require every word == 0xFFFF_FFFF, inside the same aggregate sentinel gate (fail -> drop ctx). FSBL: same word-walk (no hashing; ~570 KB of word reads, tens of ms at HSI16) after verify_images, gated by check_true_into_sentinel. Sign the lengths: V6 already carries secure/nonsecure lengths in the preimage — keep them and add the FSBL rule 'len must be a multiple of 16 and >= IMAGE_LEN_MIN', so the tail boundary is itself authenticated.
improvements.rationale: Trezor's check_image_contents re-hashes every chunk AND then verifies the rest of the flash area is uniformly 0xFF/0x00 at every boot; wf_image_upload keeps erasing until the whole target area is clean. pq1 erases the inactive slot in BEGIN, but nothing ever re-checks that the region beyond `len` is still blank at COMMIT or at boot, and in V1 the lengths are unsigned so an attacker with a signed manifest and a flipped `secure_len` controls where 'the tail' starts (the BEGIN capacity bound only stops overruns, not under-declared lengths).

improvements.title: Complete option-byte self-enforcement: pin the WRP1A/WRP2A/OEM-lock layouts, assert OEM keys cleared and BOOT_LOCK in the FSBL tripwire, and re-verify the full ship profile on EVERY post-lock boot with wipe escalation
improvements.threat: A unit whose WRP was cleared (or an OEM RDP-regression key planted) before the RDP-2 self-lock passes the tz-1 tripwire today and freezes forever with a writable FSBL — permanently forfeiting invariant #10 for that die; after lock, no code re-checks the option bytes, so an OEM-key RDP regression or SWAP_BANK flip is never noticed.
improvements.proposal: (1) Close #46: pin WRP1AR/WRP2AR/NSSR.OEMxLOCK bit layouts from RM0456 + the on-box SVD with a bench read-back receipt, flip WRP1A_MASK_PINNED/OEM_LOCK_MASK_PINNED to true so both the FSBL tripwire and first-boot Phase A fail closed on them. (2) FSBL tz-1: add `OEM1LOCK == 0 && OEM2LOCK == 0` and `SECBOOTADD0R.BOOT_LOCK == 1` (post-lock profile) to confirmed_fields_match. (3) Secure world: on every boot where RDP == L2, run verify_ship_profile (post-lock variant) before SE unlock; on mismatch trigger tzic::trigger_intrusion_wipe (dual-SE admin wipe, BHK regeneration) and halt, Trezor's secret_safety_erase semantics — a device whose protections were weakened must be useless, not merely stopped. (4) Phase A: before the RDP-2 burn, write OEM1/OEM2 key registers to 0xFFFFFFFF and assert OEMxLOCK clear so no RDP-regression key can exist post-lock (today Phase A only READS the lock status).
improvements.rationale: Trezor's boardloader compares OPTR, SECBOOTADD0R (with BOOT_LOCK), all four WRP registers and both SECWM registers against the compiled profile on every boot, erases secrets on mismatch, and additionally resets OEM keys and asserts OEMxLOCK clear. pq1 has the two-profile pattern and the read-only tripwire but deliberately skips the two registers that decide whether the FSBL is actually immutable, and first_boot returns early at RDP-2 so the post-lock state is never re-verified.

improvements.title: Adopt Trezor's Update-Control-Block invariants as explicit review rows for the Route-1 journal, and version every FSBL-consumed record so the mutable side can route around immutable-stage bugs
improvements.threat: The A/B activation path that will replace today's fail-closed COMMIT refusal re-creates the legacy try-once defects (no confirm-alive writer, both-copies-torn coerced to 'try the unproven winner', single-candidate fast path skipping arbitration), and once the FSBL is WRP+RDP-2 frozen any bug in how it consumes the journal is permanent in the field (Trezor shipped exactly such a bug: BOARDLOADER_UCB_ZERO_ADDR_BUG).
improvements.proposal: Before FA-2/#546 implementation starts, amend the Draft 1.1 Route-1 journal spec with a checklist copied from boot_ucb.c/boardloader main.c: (a) the control record is bound to the staged artifact by its SHA-256 (re-hashed by the FSBL, not trusted); (b) apply is idempotent and the record is erased as the FIRST act of the activated image; (c) the FSBL re-runs structural/CRC/digest/signature/floor on the staged candidate even though the runtime already did; (d) record validation checks magic, every address range, and non-overlap before any pointer is formed, double-checked in both producer and consumer; (e) the record carries a schema/flags byte reserved so a later mutable image can disable or reinterpret a field the frozen FSBL mis-handles; (f) confirm-alive (TRIED->COMMITTED) is written by the booted image only after a defined health milestone, never by the FSBL. Add these as named rows in the Draft 1.1 acceptance table and as fsbl-tests source_invariants pins once implemented.
improvements.rationale: pq1 already has A/B slots so 'copy' becomes 'select', but the control-record discipline transfers directly and the existing legacy arbitration violates (b), (f) and the torn-state rule. Trezor's model_T3W1.h bug is a concrete, shipped example of invariant #10's cost: the fix lives in the mutable bootloader as a workaround flag because the boardloader can never change.

improvements.title: Take the now-or-never WRP-freeze decisions as one package: Option B dual-key FSBL, immutable FSBL_MIN_ACCEPTED_FW_VERSION, vendor-pubkey OTP hash lock, and a sealed 'no secure-world update' cold-vault profile
improvements.threat: Vendor signing-key theft/coercion signs firmware that passes both verification stages on every device ever shipped, with no fleet remediation except recall; and a re-flashed FSBL today could substitute a different vendor key without refusal. Each of these levers ceases to exist the moment the FSBL freezes under WRP+RDP-2.
improvements.proposal: Schedule the freeze review now and record outcomes (even 'declined') in vendor-signing-key-compromise.md: (1) Option B — primary + recovery C10 pubkey in the FSBL (~40 B rodata + one extra verify only when the primary fails), with the recovery key's seed split-custodied offline; (2) an immutable `FSBL_MIN_ACCEPTED_FW_VERSION`/epoch constant so even a leaked primary cannot install below it; (3) #220 — burn SHA-256(vendor pubkey) into an OTP block and have the FSBL verify its embedded key against it at boot (no-op cost, closes threat-model §9.8); (4) a `mode-sealed` production profile that compiles out CMD_FW_BEGIN..ABORT dispatch (NS image remains updatable only if/when decoders move out of S-world) for a cold-vault SKU, the only option that literally refuses an extraction-enabling update. Pair with #225: per-key C10 signature cap enforced in fwsign's ledger.
improvements.rationale: The repo's own key-compromise design note identifies these as expiring decisions and recommends taking them together; the task's owner-decision list declined only cosi-style m-of-n committees, not a two-key primary/recovery FSBL. Trezor keeps 3 root keys with sigmask rotation and locks the vendor-header hash into OTP; Tangem removes the update surface entirely; pq1 currently has one baked key, no OTP lock and no floor the vendor cannot lower.

improvements.title: Merkle-batched release signing: one C10 ceremony per release covering every (board, secure, NS) artifact, with a bounded per-image proof in the unsigned manifest region
improvements.threat: Each additional signed artifact (now two boards, later revisions, plus a future PQDESC_V1 descriptor root) consumes one signature of the vendor key's finite C10 budget (OPEN-C10-1) and one HSM ceremony; today's format signs one 75/121-byte preimage per image, so the signature count scales with the artifact count and the insider/ceremony surface grows with it.
improvements.proposal: In the V6 amendment (with FWU-3): the signed value becomes a Merkle root over leaves `SHA-256(0x00 || preimage_i)` with order-independent internal nodes `SHA-256(0x01 || min || max)`; each manifest carries its own leaf preimage plus a proof path (<= 8 nodes, 32 B each) in the unsigned region; the device recomputes the root and verifies ONE C10 signature. fwsign gains a `sign-release-set` that builds the tree over all artifacts of a release set (both boards, optional descriptor-root leaf) and emits per-artifact manifests. Bound the proof length and check it fits inside the manifest page before any pointer is formed.
improvements.rationale: Trezor moved its PQ bootloader signing to exactly this structure so one slow SLH-DSA ceremony covers all models/revisions/builds, with proof size independent of batch size — directly relevant to pq1 where C10 signing is expensive, the key budget is capped, and the release set just doubled with the second board. It also gives the OPEN-REL-1 'release-set authority' a cryptographic object (the root) rather than a convention.
